title: Minimum Cost to Repair Edges to Traverse a Graph
summary: Given an undirected graph with n nodes and m edges, where each edge has a repair cost, determine the minimum cost to repair edges such that a path from node 0 to node n-1 using at most k edges is possible.
statement: Given an undirected graph with n nodes and m edges, where each edge has a repair cost, determine the minimum cost to repair edges such that a path from node 0 to node n-1 using at most k edges is possible. If it's impossible, return -1.
constraints: n≤50,000, there are up to 100,000 weighted undirected edges, and k≥1.
Choosing money repairs every edge with cost at most that threshold.
Find the minimum threshold enabling a 0-to-(n-1) path of at most k edges, or -1.
hints: For a fixed money threshold, usable edges form an unweighted graph.
Breadth-first search determines whether the destination is reachable within k edges.
This predicate is monotone as money increases, so binary-search the sorted distinct repair costs.
The first feasible threshold repairs exactly the edges needed by some allowed-length path; every smaller threshold was proved infeasible.
